mitigation_mechanism: In-field practices (zaï and tassa pits, stone bunds and stone lines, terraces, tied furrows and conservation tillage) let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the root zone, so crops suffer less in dry spells and still yield in dry years: zaï produced sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. Storage works (production cisterns, sand dams, subsurface dams, ponds and check dams) carry water into the dry season for households, livestock and supplemental irrigation and reduce reliance on water trucks or tankers, and WOCAT compilers across sheets from Niger, Burkina Faso, Kenya, Ethiopia, Tunisia, Somalia, India and other countries rate soil moisture and water availability as improved and drought impacts as reduced [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1219_2014_soil_moisture, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_water_quantity, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts].
caveats: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings of soil moisture or water availability, which are practitioner judgements and component proxies for drought impact rather than measured losses; the measured and literature units show the benefit shrinking in severe drought, with stone bunds in Burkina Faso giving no gain in the driest year and Niger families with soil and water conservation moving from surplus in good years to deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1]. Storage is bounded (most of the Kenyan sand dams studied could not supply one household through the whole dry season), a meta-analysis found no significant soil-moisture effect of infiltration trenches, an Ethiopian watershed programme showed no difference in soil water retention, and a few WOCAT sheets rate water availability or soil moisture as unchanged [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1, ev_soil_water_retention_abate21_5, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1474_2011_soil_moisture]. Storage also fails in prolonged drought, with subsurface dams in Brazil drying out in a rainless year and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limiting soil-conservation benefits; these units record no benefit rather than damage to the works, and several literature results are bundled programmes or implementer, Bank and Embrapa self-assessments [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6].

mitigation_mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and stone lines slow runoff and promote infiltration, raising soil moisture; when rainfall is erratic stone bunds conserve moisture and ease crop water stress during dry spells, and crops behind stone bunds could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Leveled fields on China's Loess Plateau increased moisture retention and broad bench terraces in semi-arid China held up to 22% more moisture than vegetated slopes, and WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone bunds in Niger, Tunisia, Bhutan, Ethiopia, Yemen, Peru, Haiti, Uzbekistan and other countries rate soil moisture as improved and drought impacts as reduced [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2, ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_2, ev_soil_water_retention_wocat_1616_2014_soil_moisture, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts].
caveats: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield benefit in the driest year and so did not reduce famine risk then, which bounds the cited dry-year gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The Loess Plateau result has no control, the Indian result is farmer perception, the Rwandan resilience finding comes from a bundled land-husbandry package, and most units are WOCAT practitioner ratings of soil moisture, a component proxy; the Haiti compiler states the drought effect has not yet been measured [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2, ev_soil_water_retention_iegind11_9, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts].

mitigation_mechanism: Contour stone bunds and stone lines, bench and progressive terraces, infiltration trenches, check dams and micro-catchments slow and spread runoff on hillslopes: terraces cut mean runoff by 50 to 98% on small mountain plots and lowered flood peaks, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment cut runoff volume by 50% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2]. WOCAT compilers across sheets from Niger, Ethiopia, Tunisia, Rwanda, China, Somalia, Jordan and other countries rate surface runoff, soil loss and downstream flooding as reduced, the Kenyan sand-dam sheet noting that a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7778_2026_surface_runoff].
caveats: Nearly all units are runoff or soil-loss measures or WOCAT practitioner ratings standing in for flood impact at plot or small-catchment scale; catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, an Uttarakhand water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent, and Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by only 3.2 percent against conventional sites [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Diversion structures can work the other way: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled the runoff coefficient and raised peak discharges, larger sand dams increase flooding risk, and check dams can cause downstream channel incision [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1]. Among the ratings, the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates flood impacts as worse, the Indian farm-pond sheet rates downstream flooding as unchanged, and the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding].

caveats: The runoff effect of trenches was much weaker on cropland (3.5%) than on land with natural vegetation (15%), and some studies found catchment sediment concentration rising in the first years after trenches were built [ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_2, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_3, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2]. The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings; their downstream-flooding ratings are mostly slight, the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates flood impacts as worse, and the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding]. Runoff and soil loss stand in for flood impact rather than measuring flood peaks.

mitigation_mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and banquettes slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces cut mean runoff by 50 to 98% and flood peaks on small mountain plots, a global study of 105 cases finds terraces on average 2.5 times more effective than slopes at reducing runoff, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment cut runoff volume by 50% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_runoff_reduction_willem21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2]. WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone bunds in Rwanda, China, Tunisia, Yemen, Peru, Haiti, Uzbekistan and other countries rate runoff, soil loss and downstream flooding as reduced, and compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand are credited with limiting damage from landslides and flood [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_flooding, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1522_2010_surface_runoff, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].
caveats: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they doubled the runoff coefficient, raised peak discharges and increased gully and bank erosion, and ditches with a downslope bank accelerate runoff and concentration time [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Abandoned terraces increase erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or never maintained, catchment-level peak-flow evidence is scarce, and most units, including the WOCAT practitioner ratings, are runoff or soil-loss proxies for flood impact [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1]. The Rwanda sediment figures and the Uttarakhand claim are Bank self-reports, and the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2].

mitigation_mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, and Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1].
caveats: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2].

mitigation_mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, and WOCAT compilers judge pits, contour bunds, stone bunds and trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm].
caveats: Most other compilers judge coping with rainstorms, thunderstorms, hailstorms or landslides as good or moderate, and those for terraces in Haiti, Thailand and Bangladesh and for marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan as very good [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm]. All units except the Loess Plateau evaluator observation are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, ripper tillage) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure. The Loess Plateau observation gives no measure of damage and ties the threat to repair funding and subsidies in adjacent areas as much as to exposure [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].
